review.title: The Coffee Khamrah
review.text: Khamrah with coffee added. Cinnamon, ginger and praline up top, then vanilla, tonka and a roasted coffee note. Fragrantica voters give it 4.32 out of 5 across 17,000+ votes, and the vast majority say winter. At about $32 it's an easy cold-weather buy, as long as you like sweet.

name: Musamam Black Intense
notesNote: Published notes as listed by Fragrantica.

review.title: The Dark Horse
review.text: Lavender, nutmeg and sage open it, then cedar, maple and cocoa-style notes. It's more aromatic and less sugary than most Lattafa picks. Rated 4.28 out of 5 on Fragrantica with 1,700+ votes, and most say winter or spring. Around $42.

name: Rugir
notesNote: Published notes as listed by Fragrantica.

review.title: The Layton Lane
review.text: Apple, lavender and bergamot over vanilla, cardamom and guaiac wood. It sits in the Parfums de Marly Layton lane at a fraction of the price. Rated 4.10 out of 5 on Fragrantica, but only 154 votes so far, so the sample is small. Around $38.

name: Terra
notesNote: Published notes as listed by Fragrantica.

review.title: The Spice Cabinet
review.text: A big spice-and-resin scent: cardamom and Sichuan pepper, then incense, amber and vanilla. Fragrantica voters rate it 4.30 out of 5 across 2,300+ votes, and most call it great value. Reviews say it's not a blind buy: the opening is divisive. Around $32 vs several hundred for Outlands.

name: Muharib
notesNote: Published notes as listed by Fragrantica.

review.title: The Honey Smoke
review.text: Lavender and lemon open into honey, cinnamon and cashmere wood, then tobacco and tonka. Rated 4.44 out of 5 on Fragrantica, the highest of this group, though from only 367 votes. About $50 and a good fit for winter nights.

review.title: The Parfum Upgrade
review.text: The Limited Edition Parfum keeps the lemon, pineapple and pepper opening people want from an Aventus-style scent, then dries down to ambroxan, musk and leather. Fragrantica voters rate it 4.44 out of 5 across 2,900+ votes, and the votes are spread across all four seasons. A good year-round pick if you want the Aventus idea in a richer, longer version.
